title: Enough for me
hook: Allah is enough for me, in Him I trust, Lord of the Throne (9:129)
tomorrow: Block A close: the long surahs

segments.voice: Yesterday: ra'uf rahim, the messenger who feels your trouble. Your line was he felt it with you. Today ends a week, and a surah.

This week, at-Tawbah. It opened with no bismillah, a silence at the door. It took you into a cave with dhat an-nitaqayn, she of the two waistbands. It called believing men and women protectors of each other. It set two mosques side by side and asked what's under the bricks. It sat with three men through fifty nights of silence, then painted a messenger who feels your trouble as his own. Now the surah's very last verse. After the battles, the excuses, the hypocrites and the forgiveness, it ends on a line a person can say at three in the morning.

Verse one hundred twenty-nine begins: and if they turn away. It imagines the worst outcome, people rejecting everything the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ has brought. And it tells him what to say. In Pickthall's translation: "Allah sufficeth me. There is no God save Him. In Him have I put my trust, and He is Lord of the Tremendous Throne." In Arabic, it starts hasbiya Allah. Hasb means enough, a sufficiency. Hasbiya: my enough. God is my enough. Notice what it doesn't say. Not that they won't turn away. Not that the plan works. It says: even if it doesn't, I'm not empty-handed. Then three steps. No god but Him, so nothing else gets that place. In Him I trust: tawakkul, leaning your whole weight. And the Throne, the Qur'an's picture of God's rule over everything. The same root runs through another phrase you may hear: hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil, God is enough for us, and the best one to rely on. Bukhari reports that Ibrahim said it when he was thrown into the fire, and the Prophet and his companions said it when they were told an army had gathered against them. Some Muslims say today's verse seven times, morning and evening, following a report in Abu Dawud that whoever does so, God will be enough for whatever worries him. A long, hard surah, full of armies and excuses, ends on one person, alone, saying: enough.
screen: `AND IF THEY TURN AWAY.` · `HASBIYA ALLAH — GOD IS MY ENOUGH.` · `NO GOD BUT HIM. IN HIM I TRUST.` · `IBRAHIM IN THE FIRE.` · then, large: `ALLAH IS ENOUGH.`

segments.voice: Let one real worry come up, the one waiting in the back of your mind, and look at it. If you pray, you can say the verse's words quietly, hasbiya Allah, God is enough for me, and let the breath out slowly after them; if you don't, notice the weight of the worry and set it down beside you for a while.
Hasbiya Allah, God is enough for me. The last verse of at-Tawbah: even if they turn away, He is enough, and in Him I trust. Today's word.
Your line: allah is enough. Even if the plan fails, you're not empty-handed. A week done, and a surah too.

howItsDone: Some Muslims recite 9:129, hasbiya Allahu la ilaha illa huwa, seven times morning and evening as part of their daily remembrance, and say hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil in moments of fear.

fork.setup: you've given everything to a message, and people turn away from it. what does the last verse of at-Tawbah tell the Prophet to say?
options: God is enough for me; in Him I trust.
leave them; they're not worth it.
fork.reveal: Allah sufficeth me. no promise the plan works, only that he isn't empty-handed if it doesn't.

original.note: Arabic: "God is enough for me," the opening of 9:129, from hasb, a sufficiency.

trapdoor: what you thought: a calming phrase.
what it means: even if everything fails, God is enough, so trust has somewhere to rest.
what a scholar hears: 9:129 closes the surah after 9:128; Abu Dawud reports the sevenfold morning and evening recitation, and the phrase echoes 3:173, hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil.

chat.says: What do Muslims mean when they say hasbiya Allah in a hard time?
options: God is enough for me; even if things go wrong, I'm not empty-handed.
God will make sure the plan works, so there's nothing to worry about.
I've given up on people, so only God is left to talk to.
chat.meaning: The verse doesn't promise the plan works. It says even if they turn away, God is enough: no god but Him, in Him I trust.

tawakkul.meaning: trust in God, leaning your whole weight on Him

Ibrahim.meaning: the prophet Abraham, who said it in the fire

Abu Dawud.meaning: compiler of a major hadith collection
